startups_draft.body:
Company Name: Sirus

URL: https://trysirus.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=first10&utm_content=startups_feedback

Purpose of Startup and Product: A free, open-source terminal workspace for developers who already have Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions and want to use them together, including multiple accounts from the same provider. Connect existing accounts, choose models and keep project memory in one place.

Technologies Used: TypeScript, React/Ink terminal interface, Node.js launcher and Bun runtime.

Feedback Requested: Does 'Your subscriptions. One terminal.' make the benefit clear, or does it sound like a billing/subscription management tool? For developers who find switching accounts or moving context between tools frustrating, what would you need to see before trying it on a small task? I'm especially interested in where account connection or model selection becomes confusing.

Seeking Beta-Testers: Yes — developers with existing subscriptions who can try a small task in a familiar project.

Additional Comments: I'm the maker and looking for first-use feedback. Sirus is MIT-licensed and needs no separate account. Provider charges and usage limits remain separate; quotas are not pooled. I've left feedback for another project here and would appreciate feedback on this positioning too. No survey or meeting required.

peer_contribution.body:
From your description, the clearest benefit is capturing the evidence during installation so the team can recover eligible labour contributions later. 'Stop doing warranty work for free' gets attention, but I'd pair it with that mechanism so it doesn't sound like guaranteed reimbursement.

A worked example showing the required evidence and what happens when a manufacturer rejects a claim would help me assess the promise. I can't judge $199/month without the team's claim volume and recoverable labour costs; a simple break-even example could make that decision easier.

setup_tip:
After sign-in, check the account shown; /usage lists saved accounts. /model changes models, while Sirus handles account routing. Start with a provider you've connected. Your subscriptions keep their own limits.
